label: French Simmental

origin.place: Franche-Comté, France, from Swiss Simmental cattle imported early in the 20th century

sources.text: French Simmental page: descends from Swiss Simmental imported at the beginning of the 20th century (no exact year); stud book opened in 1930; first bred in Franche-Comté. Simmental cattle page: the breed is named after the Simmental valley in canton Bern, Switzerland. The 1900 start of the range is taken from the 'beginning of the 20th century' wording; 1930 is the stud book date.

about.text: A dual-purpose Simmental line kept in France, used mainly for dairy and also crossbred with beef breeds. Its milk goes into the AOC cheeses Comté and Laguiole. First bred in Franche-Comté, it is now also found in Auvergne.

sources.text: Paraphrased from the French Simmental page: primarily for dairy but used for beef and milk, crossbred with Charolais and Limousin, milk used for Comté and Laguiole, first bred in Franche-Comté and now found in Auvergne.

'About 6,400 kg of milk every year' per cow, from the French Simmental page. No year or source given on the page, so no year is recorded. A French search for the Idele milk-recording figures for this breed found no breed-specific line (only an all-breed average of 8,887 kg per lactation in 2021), so that figure is not used.
Milk composition of 4% fat and 3.3% protein, from the French Simmental page. No year or method given.
The page says the breed is used 'primarily for dairy' and also for beef and milk production.

facts.v: Its milk is used for the AOC cheeses Comté and Laguiole.

sources.text: Stated on the French Simmental page.

gaps: No DAD-IS record found for the French Simmental, so no risk status. The population (about 35,000 cows, French Simmental page) is left out: the page gives no year or source, and a head record needs a year. The milk yield (about 6,400 kg a year) has no year either, so no year is recorded. No lactation length or per-lactation yield found. A French search (Idele milk recording) found no breed-specific figures in the extract seen.
